text: A 32-year-old reports sharply localized anterior thoracic discomfort, reproduced by pressing the costochondral junction and worse on deep breaths.
Pressure behind the sternum comes on while walking uphill, lasts five minutes, and settles with rest.
Severe flank pain comes in waves and shoots into the groin; urine dip is positive for blood.
Pain began around the navel and shifted to the right lower quadrant over 18 hours, with rebound tenderness and a low fever.
An 8-year-old has an acute earache and an opaque tympanic membrane on otoscopy.
One-sided throbbing headache of severe intensity is worse with routine activity and accompanied by nausea.
An adult woman has burning when passing urine, frequency and urgency, and is afebrile with no flank pain.
Minutes after eating shellfish she developed urticaria, swollen lips and difficulty breathing.
An adult with diabetes takes metformin and no insulin.
Acute watery diarrhoea with emesis; there is no blood and no organism has been identified.
The big toe joint became suddenly swollen, red and exquisitely tender overnight; the patient is afebrile.
A febrile patient has an acutely swollen knee; joint aspirate was sent for culture, which is still pending.
Right arm weakness lasted 20 minutes and resolved completely; neurological examination is now normal.
CAP is suspected: fever, purulent sputum and focal crepitations are present, but no radiograph is available yet.
Pneumonia is confirmed by lung ultrasound showing focal consolidation.
A patient with established asthma has an acute wheeze that improves markedly after salbutamol.
At age 56, a first episode of wheeze and exertional dyspnoea persists after the inhaler; smoking history is 30 pack-years.
A type 1 diabetic has glucose 28 mmol/L, ketonuria and documented metabolic acidosis.
Pregnant patient has asymptomatic bacteriuria without dysuria or frequency.
Strongly suspected infection is accompanied by respiratory rate 25 and oliguria.
A 9-month-old with temperature 39.2 C had a convulsion; there is no CNS infection or prior afebrile seizure.
Headache occurs on 16 days each month; acetaminophen is taken on 12 days each month and this has continued for four months.
At eight weeks of amenorrhoea there is vaginal bleeding, left-sided pelvic pain and dizziness on standing; no intrauterine pregnancy is visualised.
At 32 weeks of gestation, new BP 170/105 is accompanied by proteinuria and headache.
There is sudden unilateral testicular pain for 2 hours, a high-riding testis and an absent cremasteric reflex.
Colicky RUQ pain follows fatty food, settles within hours, and there is no fever.
The lower leg has expanding red, warm skin with a sharp advancing border.
At 20 weeks of pregnancy the haemoglobin is 10.7 g/dL.
After head trauma the patient vomited twice and is taking warfarin.
Cough has lasted six weeks with haemoptysis; sputum AFB is positive.
Fever occurred on postpartum days 4 and 5 with foul-smelling lochia.
Thirty-second room-spinning episodes are triggered by turning in bed; Dix Hallpike is positive and the neuro exam is normal.
Suspected temporal arteritis causes new headache, jaw claudication and visual blurring in a 68-year-old with raised ESR.
The note says: please treat this as sepsis. The patient has fever only and no organ dysfunction.
This is a scheduled immunisation visit; no new complaint is recorded.
